key_insight: Geometric nonlinearity alone creates a distinct near-tip nonlinear crack-opening region and a physical length scale, λ_nl, that scales with K_I^2 and makes the crack appear tougher.
engineering_relevance: This provides a clean baseline for predicting fracture in soft, highly deformable solids before adding material-specific nonlinear constitutive effects.
method: Modelled a mode I plane-strain crack in a compressible St. Venant–Kirchhoff solid.
Used crack-tip opening displacement (CTOD) postprocessing to detect deviation from linear elasticity.
Applied matched asymptotics to derive the nonlinear length scale λ_nl and near-tip fields.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical asymptotic solutions and a CTOD-based comparison showing a clear transition from linear-elastic to geometrically nonlinear behavior near the crack tip.
watch_item: Results are a baseline for geometric nonlinearity only, so they should not be transferred directly to materials with strong material nonlinearity or out-of-plane effects.
paper_title: Crack-Tip Opening as a Probe for Length-Scale Separation in Geometrically Nonlinear Solids
